bib.title: Large Language Models Struggle to Learn Long-Tail Knowledge

question: How does an LLM's ability to answer a factoid question depend on how many pre-training documents are relevant to that question?
hypothesis: Plainly implied: models mainly succeed on knowledge that appears widely in pre-training data, so accuracy rises with relevant document count and rare facts are learned poorly.
contributions: Entity-linking pipeline over trillions of tokens (C4, Pile, ROOTS, OpenWebText, Wikipedia) that counts documents where question and answer entities co-occur
Correlational study of QA accuracy vs relevant document count across BLOOM, GPT-Neo, GPT-3
Counterfactual re-training of a 4.8B LM with relevant documents removed
Analysis of dataset scaling, model scaling and retrieval augmentation for long-tail knowledge
Release of code and entity data

method.summary: Entity-link pre-training corpora and QA sets, count documents containing both the salient question entity and answer entity, and plot few-shot closed-book exact-match accuracy of open LLMs against that count. A 4.8B LM is retrained on C4 with relevant documents removed to test causality, and oracle and BM25 retrieval are added to see if they remove the dependence.
method.task: closed-book factoid open-domain QA, analysed against pre-training data frequency

datasets.name: TriviaQA
datasets.split: train and validation combined, except a small set held out for few-shot prompts
datasets.preprocessing: Entity linked with DBpedia Spotlight; question and all answers concatenated; most common answer entity is salient answer entity; question entity with most co-occurrence with it chosen; examples with no entity or zero relevant documents discarded

datasets.name: Natural Questions
datasets.split: train and validation combined, except a small set held out for few-shot prompts

datasets.name: C4
datasets.preprocessing: entity linked; also used to train the 4.8B baseline and counterfactual LMs

datasets.name: OpenWebText
datasets.preprocessing: entity linked; used to estimate GPT-3 counts by scaling

datasets.name: Wikipedia (Dec 2018 dump)
datasets.preprocessing: entity linked; knowledge corpus for BM25 retrieval

other.caveat: training data not public; counts estimated by scaling OpenWebText counts; sizes approximate; fine-tuning status uncertain; results in Appendix

models.name: Baseline and counterfactual LM
models.architecture: decoder-only (inferred: follows Wang et al. 2022 setup)

training.steps: counterfactual model trained for 30% fewer steps than baseline; absolute steps not stated

other.setup: baseline 4.8B LM on C4 following Wang et al. (2022); counterfactual removes all relevant documents of 100 sampled TriviaQA questions per log-scaled count bin, about 30% of C4
other.note: Only the 4.8B retraining trains anything; hyperparameters deferred to Wang et al. 2022

inference.samples: one greedy answer per question; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: 4-shot closed-book 'Q: ... A: ...' template (other shot counts gave similar trends); 2-shot for oracle retrieval
inference.retrieval: oracle: 300-word segment around the ground-truth answer in the gold Wikipedia page; BM25: top-3 Wikipedia paragraphs in prompt for in-context examples and test question, each in-context example checked to have the answer in at least one paragraph

metrics.name: Exact Match QA accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match against ground-truth answer set, averaged over log-spaced bins of relevant document count; bins under 500 examples trimmed from plots

metrics.name: BM25 top-k recall
metrics.definition: recall of the answer-bearing document in top k

metrics.name: Human accuracy
metrics.definition: leave-one-annotator-out on NQ questions with 5 raters, with background text

eval.protocol: Correlation plots over log-spaced bins; no significance tests or seeds reported; precision of document counting checked by manual labelling of 300 TriviaQA pairs

availability.data: entity data for ROOTS, The Pile, C4, OpenWebText, Wikipedia released at same URL

results.setup: 300 random TriviaQA pairs, one random relevant doc each, manually labelled: 33% enough to answer, additional 27% some relevant info

results.quote: BLOOM-176B has over 4× higher accuracy than BLOOM-560M on

results.claim: Removing relevant documents from C4 for a retrained 4.8B LM lowers accuracy mainly on questions with many original relevant documents, indicating a causal link.
results.setup: 4.8B LM trained on C4 one epoch; 100 TriviaQA questions per log bin; about 30% of C4 removed; counterfactual trained 30% fewer steps
results.quote: In total, this removes about 30% of C4.

results.claim: A log-linear fit of BLOOM accuracy on rare NQ questions implies over 10^18 parameters to match supervised or human accuracy.
results.setup: BLOOM, Natural Questions, questions with fewer than 100 relevant docs; fit R2 = 0.98; train+validation used for the trend, validation for baselines
results.quote: one would need a BLOOM model with over 1018
results.note: Text extraction renders 10^18 as '1018'; abstract says 'many orders of magnitude', intro cites one quadrillion parameters.

results.claim: Scaling datasets by moderate factors (e.g. 5x) gives small accuracy gains; relevant counts are highly rank-correlated across pre-training corpora.
results.setup: Spearman correlation of TriviaQA relevant doc counts across ROOTS, Pile, C4, OWT, Wikipedia: 0.87 to 0.97

results.setup: GPT-Neo, Natural Questions, 2-shot, 300-word gold Wikipedia segment

results.claim: BM25 top-3 retrieval raises GPT-Neo accuracy over closed-book at all count ranges, especially rare ones, though BM25 recall still depends mildly on count.
results.setup: GPT-Neo, Natural Questions, BM25 over Wikipedia, top-3 paragraphs
results.quote: We add the top-3 highest scoring para-

results.claim: Counting only question or only answer entity does not correlate with accuracy when Q-A entities co-occur fewer than 5 times, supporting the co-occurrence definition.
Humans show the opposite trend from LMs: highest accuracy on questions with few relevant documents, so low counts are not simply harder questions.
results.setup: Natural Questions, leave-one-annotator-out, 5 raters with background text

results.claim: Entity linking 2.1TB of pre-training data took about 3 weeks on a 128-CPU-core machine.

limits: Document counting is imperfect: about 60% precision on TriviaQA, plus entity-linker errors and unknown recall; examples with zero relevant documents were discarded as linker errors.
Co-occurrence of two entities is a proxy for the fact being stated, not proof.
GPT-3 results rest on estimated counts from OpenWebText, uncertain sizes and unknown fine-tuning; moved to Appendix.
Only factoid QA studied (TriviaQA, NQ); authors leave open whether other tasks show the same relation.
The causal experiment uses one 4.8B model trained for one epoch; the counterfactual had 30% fewer steps, so only removed-question accuracy is compared.
Scaling extrapolation (over 10^18 parameters) is a log-linear fit across a limited model range, with R2 0.97 to 0.99; the degree changes by setup (App B).
BM25 retrieval with Wikipedia; no dense retriever or modern RAG pipelines tested; models are 2022-era base LMs, not instruction-tuned chat models.
Hyperparameters of the 4.8B retraining are not given beyond a pointer to Wang et al. 2022.
